substantive_definition_1881: Hereditary caste status treated as synonymous with livelihood; conflated hill Khatris/Rajputs with plains pastoralists
substantive_definition_1931: Separated principal earners from working dependents; Gaddi listed as caste while pastoralism listed as industry sector
substantive_definition_1961: Disaggregates primary occupation (Cultivation) from subsidiary transhumance; enumerates exact flock sizes (4,484 sheep/goats)
comparability_rationale_and_limits: 1881 conflates caste and work; 1931 isolates economic activity; 1961 captures multi-tiered seasonal livelihoods. Direct trendlines invalid.

substantive_definition_1881: Assumed all individuals of landowning castes were agriculturalists; paternal occupation ascribed to entire lineage
substantive_definition_1931: Separated cultivating owners from rent-receiving landlords and tenant farmers under Great Depression pressures
substantive_definition_1961: Detailed primary occupation table (p. 37) recording near gender parity (116 male vs 114 female cultivators in Brahmaur)
comparability_rationale_and_limits: 1881 ascribes agriculture by caste; 1931 classifies by tenurial contract; 1961 records actual active field workers.

substantive_definition_1881: Counted under menial impure castes; ploughing labour treated as hereditary low-caste service obligation
substantive_definition_1931: Enumerated as wage-earning or dependent agricultural labourers; caste identity often submerged under political mobilization
substantive_definition_1961: Micro-survey records exact households (2 hh in Chitrari) and explicit transition from customary servitude to Arya Samaj reform
comparability_rationale_and_limits: 1881 views Halis as hereditary menials; 1931 as economic wage hands; 1961 reveals active political and religious identity contestation.

substantive_definition_1881: Counted strictly under hereditary artisanal caste category Lohar
substantive_definition_1931: Listed under Industry (Metalworkers) with earners disaggregated from dependents
substantive_definition_1961: Micro-census records 2 households in Maingal operating under non-monetary khalian grain barter from threshing floors
comparability_rationale_and_limits: Highly stable technical craft category across all periods; 1961 uniquely documents persistence of non-monetary jajmani exchange.

category_1881: Hill Weavers & Impure Menials (Sipi / Koli / Badi)
substantive_definition_1881: Conflated under generic impure hill menials; Ibbetson acknowledges inability to cleanly separate Sipi from Hali or Koli
substantive_definition_1931: Submerged under generic industrial textile categories; ethnic and ritual specificity completely lost
substantive_definition_1961: Micro-census provides precise village enumeration (15 hh / 119 pop in Brahmaur) and tripartite role (shearer, weaver, ritual drummer)
comparability_rationale_and_limits: Colonial censuses aggregated or obscured Sipis into generic categories; only 1961 micro-data recovers their specific tripartite economic-ritual niche.

category_1931: Pastoralists by Religion (Muslim vs Hindu Gujjars)
category_1961_micro: Settled Buffalo Herders & Transhumant Traders (Muslim Gujjars)
substantive_definition_1881: Conflated transhumant alpine buffalo keepers with sedentary plains agriculturalists; loaded with criminal stereotypes
substantive_definition_1931: Enumerated by religion and broad pastoral class; February census timing caught transhumants in Kangra winter camps
substantive_definition_1961: Micro-census in Maingal captures permanent settled hamlets owning 217 buffaloes, alongside seasonal visits to Chitrari dhars
comparability_rationale_and_limits: Severe enumeration artifacts caused by census seasonality (winter plains vs summer hills); 1961 captures sedentary forest hamlets.

substantive_definition_1881: Classified entire Brahmin caste as priestly class regardless of actual engagement in cultivation or administration
substantive_definition_1931: Enumerated individuals actively earning primary livelihood from religious service, excluding landed rentiers
substantive_definition_1961: Demonstrates that 77% of Chitrari is Brahmin, where sacred temple status legitimised vast landed estates and agrarian tenancy
comparability_rationale_and_limits: 1881 assumes all Brahmins are priests; 1931 restricts to religious practitioners; 1961 demonstrates Brahmins functioned primarily as landed proprietors.

category_1881: Unfree Corvee Labour (Begar / Customary State Dues)
category_1931: Abolished / Regulated Princely State Labour Dues
category_1961_micro: Abolished Feudal Memory / Voluntary Wage Labour
substantive_definition_1881: Begar treated as customary sovereign right of Chamba Raja; completely excluded from wage labour statistics
substantive_definition_1931: Begar legally restricted under colonial indirect rule; absent from standard provincial occupational tables
substantive_definition_1961: Completely illegal and absent from 1961 occupational tables; preserved only in oral memory and historical chapters
comparability_rationale_and_limits: Fundamental transformation of sovereign and legal regime; cannot be compared across census tables as an occupational category.
